newsitem.title: FINLAND: Lira-ERM talk boosts pressure on Finland -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Lira-ERM talk boosts pressure on Finland -analysts.

text.p: Italy's intention to quickly link the lira to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) is raising the pressure on Finland which has been hesitant to peg its recently strong markka to ERM, analysts said on Thursday.

"It has been known for quite some time that Italy aims to go back in soon. This makes it more urgent for us, too," said Jussi Mustonen, chief economist at the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT).

Finland has low inflation and long-term interest rates and a strong chance of meeting the public sector deficit and debt criteria for a single currency, and it has argued it should not be left out of EMU just because it may not join ERM.
But Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto on Wednesday said he now believed ERM membership would be a must to join Economic and Monetary Union, which some analysts linked to Italy's situation.
Finnish bank Postipankki has repeatedly said it believes Germany is far from eager to see Italy joining the third phase of EMU in the first wave in 1999.

"If one wanted to exclude Italy ... then ERM may become the only criterion the Italians have failed to meet," said Postipankki chief economist Ari Aaltonen. If Finland were also out of ERM, that would put its EMU participation at risk.
"Finland should rather join ERM before Italy," he said -- it could become vital for Finland to have been in ERM longer than Italy.
Economist John Rogers at the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) said pressures would certainly build on Finland to join ERM if the lira went in before the markka.
"Speculation could increase about when Finland will ultimately join, and amid this speculation the markka might strengthen -- and this could lead to even bigger pressures," Rogers said.
"It could be better from Finland's point of view to join (ERM) at the same time as Italy," he said.
Central Chamber of Commerce economist Jukka Kero said he would not be surprised if the markka and the lira were pegged to ERM at the same time.
"It would certainly not reduce the pressure on Finland if Italy joined before us," he said.
Kero, unlike many financial market economists, no longer saw much scope for the markka to strengthen further.

"Economic fundamentals will not really improve much more. Inflation will inevitably accelerate, at least slightly, and the current account trend will not get better so the markka should not be under any great strengthening pressure," he said.
He said that if Finland wanted a peg at slightly weaker central parity rates than currently it might make sense to wait until later in the autumn.
Finnish industry has expressed reservations about the markka being pegged to ERM at a too strong exchange rate.
TT's Mustonen said it would be preferable for ERM entry not to become the crux as EU leaders decide in spring 1998 which countries may join EMU from the start.
Looking at how Finland and Italy were positioned on the other EMU entry criteria, Italy was in more of a hurry to link, he said. "Finland has better overall stability."
